segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see that the kingdom of God has come with power.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After six days Jesus took Peter, James and John and led them up a high mountain by themselves, alone. And he was transformed in front of them,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and his clothes became dazzling white, far whiter than any launderer on earth could make them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter spoke up and said to Jesus,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Rabbi, it is good that we are here. Let us make three tents: one for you, one for Moses and one for Elijah.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For he did not know what to say, because they were terrified.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then a cloud came and overshadowed them, and a voice came from the cloud:

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Suddenly, when they looked around, they no longer saw anyone with them but Jesus alone.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As they were coming down from the mountain, he ordered them to tell no one what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They kept the matter to themselves, discussing what this rising from the dead meant.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they asked him,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Elijah does come first and restores all things. Yet how is it written of the Son of Man that he must suffer much and be treated with contempt?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But I tell you that Elijah has indeed come, and they did to him whatever they wished, just as it is written of him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they came to the disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As soon as the whole crowd saw him, they were struck with amazement and ran up to greet him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He asked them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What are you arguing about with them?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of the crowd answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has a mute spirit,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and wherever it seizes him it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth and goes rigid. I asked your disciples to drive it out, and they could not.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In reply he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “O unbelieving generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him to me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they brought the boy to him. When the spirit saw Jesus, it at once threw the boy into convulsions, and he fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus asked his father,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “How long has this been happening to him?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “From childhood.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: It has often thrown him into fire and into water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “‘If you can’! All things are possible for the one who believes.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At once the child’s father cried out,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I believe; help my unbelief!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus saw that a crowd was quickly gathering, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Mute and deaf spirit, I command you: come out of him and never enter him again.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It cried out, convulsed him violently and came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that most of them said he was dead.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him, and he stood up.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus had gone indoors, his disciples asked him privately,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Why could we not drive it out?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This kind can come out by nothing except prayer.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They left that place and were passing through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for he was teaching his disciples and telling them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The Son of Man is being handed over into human hands, and they will kill him, and after he has been killed, three days later he will rise.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they did not understand what he said, and they were afraid to ask him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came to Capernaum. When he was in the house, he asked them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What were you discussing on the way?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they kept silent, for on the way they had argued with one another about who was the greatest.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He sat down, called the Twelve and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If anyone wants to be first, he must be last of all and servant of all.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he took a child and stood it among them, and taking it in his arms he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me welcomes not me but the one who sent me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: John said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do not stop him, for no one who does a work of power in my name will be able soon afterward to speak evil of me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For whoever is not against us is for us.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you belong to Christ, truly I tell you, he will certainly not lose his reward.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a great millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than, having two hands, to go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than, having two feet, to be thrown into Gehenna.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than, having two eyes, to be thrown into Gehenna,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For everyone will be salted with fire.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Salt is good; but if the salt becomes unsalty, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

notes.note: The Greek verb is the ordinary word for a change of form or appearance, and Paul uses it for the change in believers (Romans 12:2; 2 Corinthians 3:18), where it is normally translated 'transformed'. 'Transfigured' comes from the Latin translation and is now used in English almost only for this event. Most translations keep 'transfigured'; the plain word is used here because it is what a Greek reader heard.

The word means a tent or temporary shelter. It is the Septuagint's word both for the wilderness tabernacle and for the booths of the autumn Feast of Booths, so Peter's proposal may carry festival or wilderness overtones. Why he offers it is not explained; Mark says only that he did not know what to say.

notes.phrase: They kept the matter to themselves
notes.note: The Greek phrase 'to themselves' can go with either verb. The alternative reading is 'They held on to what he said, discussing among themselves what this rising from the dead meant.' Both are grammatical and translations are divided.

The expectation rests on the closing lines of Malachi, where God promises to send the prophet Elijah before the day of the Lord. Having just seen Elijah on the mountain, the disciples ask how this fits. Jesus' answer that Elijah 'has indeed come' and was mistreated is generally understood to point to John the Baptist, as Matthew's parallel says outright.

The earliest manuscripts carried no breathing marks, and here the pronoun can be read either as 'them' or as a reflexive, 'among yourselves'. The SBLGNT prints the reflexive form; most editions and translations read 'with them', which matches verse 14 and is followed here. It is also unclear whether Jesus is addressing the crowd, the scribes or the disciples.

In the earliest text Jesus picks up the father's own words from verse 22 and throws them back as an exclamation. Later manuscripts added 'believe', which produces the familiar older rendering 'If you can believe, all things are possible'. Modern editions and translations follow the shorter text.

Most later manuscripts read 'by prayer and fasting'. A small number of early and important witnesses lack 'and fasting', and the SBLGNT, like most modern editions, judges the words a later addition reflecting church practice. The decision is not unanimous among scholars, since the manuscript support for the longer reading is very wide.
The Greek specifies a 'donkey millstone': the large upper stone of a mill turned by a donkey, as opposed to a small hand mill. The point is its crushing weight.

Gehenna is a place name, the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, which had become in Jewish usage a name for the place of final judgment. 'Hell' merges it with Hades, the realm of the dead, and with much later imagery. Many translations still use 'hell', usually with a footnote giving Gehenna; several modern ones keep the name.

notes.phrase: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched
notes.note: The words echo the last verse of Isaiah (66:24), which describes the corpses of those who rebelled against God. Later manuscripts repeat this sentence after verses 43 and 45, where older English Bibles number it as verses 44 and 46. The earliest witnesses have it only here, so modern editions omit those two verses and the numbering skips them.

Many later manuscripts add 'and every sacrifice will be salted with salt', an echo of Leviticus 2:13, probably added to explain a difficult saying. The meaning of the short form is disputed. Common suggestions are that fire stands for testing or purifying that every disciple must undergo, or for judgment, with salt recalling its use on sacrifices.
